blueprint_concepts: Basic elements of the standard hyperbola: focus, directrix, axis, latus rectum
hyperbola with axis parallel to a coordinate axis (shifted form)
english: Let $\lambda$ be a real number such that the equation $16x^{2}-9y^{2}-32x-36y+\lambda=0$ represents a hyperbola having one of its foci at the point $(1,3)$. Then the area of the rectangle whose vertices are the end points of the two latera recta of this hyperbola is ______.
hindi: माना $\lambda$ एक ऐसी वास्तविक संख्या है कि समीकरण $16x^{2}-9y^{2}-32x-36y+\lambda=0$ एक ऐसे अतिपरवलय को निरूपित करता है जिसकी एक नाभि बिन्दु $(1,3)$ पर है। तब उस आयत का क्षेत्रफल, जिसके शीर्ष इस अतिपरवलय के दोनों नाभिलम्बों के अन्त्य बिन्दु हैं, ______ है।
solution: Focus $(1,3)$ is on $x=1$, so the transverse axis is vertical: $\dfrac{(y+2)^{2}}{K/9}-\dfrac{(x-1)^{2}}{K/16}=1$ with $K=20+\lambda>0$
Latera recta: $y=3$ and $y=-7$, each of length $\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{9}{2}$
solution_full: A focus lies on the transverse axis through $C$. The focus $(1,3)$ lies on the line $x=1$, so the transverse axis is vertical, and the equation must have the form $9(y+2)^{2}-16(x-1)^{2}=K$ with $K=20+\lambda>0$, i.e. $\dfrac{(y+2)^{2}}{K/9}-\dfrac{(x-1)^{2}}{K/16}=1$.

Here $a^{2}=\dfrac{K}{9}$ (along $y$) and $b^{2}=\dfrac{K}{16}$. The distance from the centre to the focus is $c=3-(-2)=5$, so $a^{2}+b^{2}=25$: $\dfrac{25K}{144}=25$, giving $K=144$ and $\lambda=124$.

The latera recta are the focal chords perpendicular to the transverse axis: the lines $y=3$ and $y=-7$. Each has length $\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{18}{4}=\dfrac{9}{2}$, with end points $\left(1\pm\dfrac{9}{4},3\right)$ and $\left(1\pm\dfrac{9}{4},-7\right)$.
These four points form a rectangle of sides $\dfrac{9}{2}$ and $3-(-7)=10$, so its area is $45$.
originality_note: New: the unknown constant of a shifted hyperbola is fixed by the position of a focus (which also decides that the transverse axis is vertical), and the rectangle of the latus-rectum ends is measured (way 5). Closest known: finding centre, foci and latus rectum of a given shifted hyperbola such as 16x^2 - 9y^2 + 32x + 36y - 164 = 0. Different because: the constant is unknown and the sign of the right side, hence the orientation, must be deduced from the focus.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard hyperbola: Focus distance c = 5 with c^2 = a^2 + b^2, the latus rectum length 2b^2/a and the latus recta through the foci give the rectangle.
concept_use.hyperbola with axis parallel to a coordi: Completing squares gives the shifted form with centre (1, -2); the focus on x = 1 shows the transverse axis is parallel to the y-axis.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and symbol is introduced, every condition is stated, there is one reading of each sentence; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no asymptote wording. Checked that lambda is unique (a horizontal transverse axis cannot have a focus at (1,3)) and that 'the two latera recta' and the rectangle are unambiguous. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising from the focus that the transverse axis is vertical, then c = 5 fixes K = 144.
justification: Routine multi-step chain: complete squares, decide orientation, use c^2 = a^2 + b^2, latus rectum. No insight needed; numerical format. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q4 (L2) on a hyperbola and 2026-P2-Q17 (L2).
